objective_for_doctor: A 35-year-old F patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: purulent nasal discharge.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve had greenish or yellowish nasal discharge, along with a cough and a cold in the last 2 weeks. I also have burning and sharp pain rated 5/10 in my forehead, left cheek, nose, left eye, and right temple, and it radiates to the back of my head.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—can you confirm: do you have fever (≥38°C), facial swelling, and does the pain worsen when you bend forward? Also, is the nasal discharge foul-smelling or mostly from one side?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Nasal/sinus exam and vitals; consider requesting Sinus_X-ray or CT if severe/one-sided or not improving.

I don’t know. I don’t know about fever (≥38°C), facial swelling, or whether the pain worsens when I bend forward. I also don’t know if the nasal discharge is foul-smelling or mostly from one side.

I do have greenish or yellowish nasal discharge and I’ve had a cold in the last 2 weeks, along with a cough.

Doctor: I’m going to ask a few key questions to narrow this down—do you have tooth pain (upper teeth), worsening one-sided facial pain, or symptoms of allergy (itchy eyes/sneezing) rather than a typical infection? Also, is the discharge thick/post-nasal drip with cough mainly at night?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Vitals (T), and if possible a focused nasal/sinus exam (tenderness, unilateral discharge, erythema), plus CBC if fever or severe symptoms.

I don’t know.  

I do have polyps in my nose and a deviated nasal septum, and I’m more likely to develop common allergies than the general population. I also have greenish or yellowish nasal discharge and a cough.

Doctor: I understand—given 2 weeks of thick green/yellow discharge with facial pressure/pain and your nasal polyps/deviated septum, this fits **acute rhinosinusitis**, but I need 2 quick answers: do you have fever (≥38°C) or clear worsening of facial pain when bending forward? Also, is the discharge mainly **one-sided** or truly both sides?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Vitals (T) and focused sinus/nasal exam for unilateral purulence and tenderness (consider CBC only if fever or severe), and if not improving after 10 days or if severe: REQUEST TEST: CT_Orbits/Sinuses.
I don’t know about fever (≥38°C) or whether my facial pain gets worse when I bend forward. I also don’t know if the discharge is mainly one-sided or truly both sides.

Doctor: I’ll examine you now—on exam I’m checking your nasal cavity for unilateral purulence, visible polyps, and sinus tenderness (percussion/pressing the maxillary/frontal areas).  
Doctor: While I do that, can you answer just one thing: is the pain and discharge mostly on the **left side** (yes/no)?  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute rhinosinusitis (likely bacterial) on a background of nasal polyps/deviated septum.
